companies.name: Kusumgar Limited
companies.oneLiner: Since 1970 — niche technical-fabric maker for parachutes, defence gear and industrial use; about half its sales are exports, with healthy ~25% margins.

fit.reason: Profitable with ~25% margins, a 44% five-year revenue growth rate, and diversified customers.

snapshot.whatTheyDo: Kusumgar makes specialised technical fabrics — the high-performance cloth used in parachutes, military gear, conveyor belts and outdoor brands. It designs and makes everything in-house and sells about half of it abroad, mostly to the US.
businessBullets: Four lines: Defence Fabrics, Defence Solutions, Auto & Industrial, Outdoor
1,000+ products; ~30 new products launched a month
Clients: Airborne Systems, Toray, Crye Precision, Aditya Birla

management.name: Ankur Kothari
management.note: ex-COO Arvind, ex-BCG · IIT Delhi, Kellogg · joined 2019

snapshot.ownershipNote: Promoter-owned; 2.5% employee ESOP pool over 10-yr vesting. Detailed cap table to be received.

segments.note: Defence-linked fabrics and solutions drive the mix; auto & industrial adds ballast.

fitChecklist.label: Cash generative
fitChecklist.note: Free cash flow to be confirmed

fitChecklist.label: Low customer concentration
fitChecklist.note: Diversified mix; no single dominant customer

integrity.finding: FY24 filings show a ₹32 cr royalty expense — nature to be clarified

items: Two lines (Defence fabric & Products) are 64% of FY25 revenue but set to de-grow in FY26 — what's the signed/advanced order book?
Safran ~98% wallet share and Airborne ~35–40% — how lumpy are revenues and margins by customer?
Customer-level history, past and future?
Historical order-conversion ratios and timelines by segment?
Win/loss rates and RFQ expiry?
60% of raw material is imported — how has price volatility been managed historically?
Capacity and utilisation by segment?
Capex done in the last 3 years and planned capex?
Key competitors by segment and our differentiation (technology / quality / pricing)?
FY24 MCA filings show a ₹32 cr royalty expense — what is it?

thesis.detail: ~25% EBITDA margins with real pricing power (parachute material margins 70–75%).
Half of sales are exports; scope to grow Airborne wallet share from ~15% toward 60%.
Full weaving-to-lamination stack; ~30 new products launched a month.
DRHP filing underway; listing targeted by early 2026.

concerns.mitigant: Broaden customer base; get customer-level order history.

concerns.issue: Big lines set to de-grow in FY26
concerns.detail: 64% of FY25 revenue in lines expected to shrink.

concerns.mitigant: Clarify purpose and whether it recurs.
Professional CEO (ex-Arvind/BCG) in place; strengthen the board.

companies.name: Attero Recycling Private Limited
companies.oneLiner: India's largest e-waste recycler (since 2008) — recovers metals from old electronics and lithium-ion batteries, and sells recycling credits to big brands like LG, HP and Sony.

fit.reason: Clear category leader growing fast, but margins are thin and free cash flow stays negative until FY28.

snapshot.whatTheyDo: Attero collects old electronics and used lithium-ion batteries, breaks them down, and extracts pure metals (copper, iron, aluminium) to sell back into the market. It also earns 'recycling credits' (EPR) from big brands that are required to recycle their waste.
businessBullets: Buys waste from OEMs, aggregators (kabadiwalas) and bulk users
Recovers & refines metals at its Roorkee plant
Sells metals on long-term contracts + earns EPR credits
Brand contracts: LG, HP, Sony, Whirlpool, Godrej, Daikin

promoters.name: Nitin Gupta
promoters.note: IIT Delhi, NYU Stern · 23+ yrs · ex-Lotus Interworks, Ittiam

management.name: Gaurav Gupta
management.note: ex-YES Bank · IIT Delhi, IIM-L · 18+ yrs

segments.note: The E-waste core scales while lithium-ion + black-mass become the growth engine from FY27.

fitChecklist.label: Profitable (historically)
fitChecklist.note: Yes, apart from a one-off ₹76 cr EPR write-off in FY25

fitChecklist.label: Cash generative
fitChecklist.note: Free cash flow negative until FY28 (heavy capex)

fitChecklist.label: Market leadership
fitChecklist.note: Largest e-waste recycler; next player ~1/3 the size

fitChecklist.label: Low customer concentration
fitChecklist.note: Metals sold in open market; EPR income may concentrate

fitChecklist.label: Raised institutional capital before
fitChecklist.note: TPG, Kalaari, Granite Hill and others on the cap table

integrity.finding: Promoted & managed by the Gupta family; clean background
One lawsuit; paid ~₹3 mn compensation for supplying damaged products

thesis.point: Clear category leader in a growing market
thesis.detail: India's e-waste roughly doubles every five years; Attero is the largest recycler, ~3× the next player.
In-house refining, PCB recycling and one of the largest sets of EPR contracts with Tier-1 brands.
Large e-waste capacity expansion (144k→594k MTPA) plus a fast-growing battery / black-mass business.
Investing ahead of a planned listing.

concerns.mitigant: Scale and a richer battery mix expected to lift margins above 20%.

concerns.issue: Negative free cash flow until FY28
concerns.mitigant: Capex is front-loaded; cash flow turns positive as utilisation ramps.
Understand the cause and whether it can recur before pricing.
Metalmandi/Salesmart to bring ~50% of sourcing in-house by FY28.

peers.note: Most e-waste recyclers earn single-digit/low-teens EBITDA margins; TES-AMM is the profitable outlier. Attero is the clear scale leader (~3x the next player).

peerBenchmark.note: Most e-waste recyclers earn single-digit/low-teens EBITDA margins; Attero is the scale leader but its FY24 margin is still thin.

companies.name: Nexon Omniverse Limited (Style Union)
companies.oneLiner: Fast-fashion value retailer (100+ stores across South India) with a no-discount model and higher-than-peer margins; led by ex-Future Group veterans.

transaction.headline: Up to ₹400 cr — primary growth capital

fit.reason: Explosive growth, but still loss-making and the promoter's governance history needs a closer look.

snapshot.whatTheyDo: Style Union is a fast-fashion value retailer — over 100 stores across South India selling affordable men's, women's and kids' clothing that refreshes every week. It never discounts, which keeps margins higher than rivals, and it's run by veterans of the old Future Group.
businessBullets: 100+ stores across 5 South-Indian states; entering West India
No-discount model → 45% gross margin (~10% above peers)
App with 3.8 lakh downloads; online + offline

promoters.name: Rakesh Biyani
promoters.note: ex-Jt MD Future Retail, ex-Chairman Future Supply Chain · founded Style Union 2022

snapshot.ownershipNote: Majority owned by the Biyani family. Backers include family offices (Taparia, Piyush Goyal); Metta invested ₹195 cr in 2022. Full cap table to be received.

fitChecklist.label: Cash generative
fitChecklist.note: Free cash flow negative until FY27

integrity.finding: Promoter was Chairman of the now-defunct Future Group — governance history to diligence

thesis.point: Explosive growth off a differentiated model
thesis.detail: No-discount, weekly-refresh value fashion with ~45% gross margins (~10% above peers).
A bench of ex-Future Group retail veterans.
Path from ~1% EBITDA (FY25) toward low-teens by FY28 as stores mature.
India value-apparel ~₹3.9 lakh cr, growing ~16% a year.

concerns.detail: Negative profit and cash flow until FY27.
concerns.mitigant: Store cohort economics are improving; watch the maturity curve.
